name: Sika Firerate
paste:
SIKA® FIRERATE: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Firerate, July 2025, Version 01.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/3/sika_firerate.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Firerate where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.04).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Firerate is an intumescent fire rated, 1-component, acrylic joint sealant.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sika® Firerate is designed for fire rated movement and connection joints on porous and non-porous substrates. It is suitable for interior applications.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.9.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Firerate
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: FIRE RATED JOINT SEALANT
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - AS 1530.4 FRL
    - ISO 717.1 Rw (Ctr) = 64 (-13)
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1530.4: cited elsewhere in the data sheet; listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1); Features (p.1).
    - ISO 717.1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.1).
    - CQP 049-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Curing rate (p.2).
    - CQP 019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Skinning time (p.2).
    - AS 1530.4:2014: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Further Documentation > FURTHER DOCUMENTS (p.2).
    - AS/ISO 717.4:2004: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Further Documentation > FURTHER DOCUMENTS (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Up to 4 hours fire resistance according to AS 1530.4
    - Very good resistance to weathering
    - Movement capability of ±20 %
    - Intumescent, expands when exposed to fire or heat above 90°C
    - Easy to smooth and very good workability
    - Good adhesion to many different substrates
    - Water clean-up of uncured sealant
    - Can be painted over using water based paints
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: 1-component acrylic dispersion
    - Colour: Grey
    - Density: ~1.45 kg/l
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: ~30 (after 28 days) (EN ISO 868)
    - Movement capability: ±20 %
2.7 Service temperature.
    | Maximum | +80°C |
    | Minimum | −20°C |
2.8 Joint design. The joint width must be designed to suit the joint movement required and the movement capability of the sealant. The joint width shall be ≥ 10 mm and ≤ 50 mm. The joint depth shall be ≤ 10 mm. A width to depth ratio of 2:1 must be maintained. All joints must be correctly designed and dimensioned in accordance with the relevant standards, before their construction. The basis for calculation of the necessary joint widths are the type of structure and its dimensions, the technical values of the adjacent building materials and the joint sealing material, as well as the specific exposure of the building and the joints. Note: Test certificates should be referred to while designing a firerated joint
2.9 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 600ml foil pack, 15 foil packs per carton; 300 ml cartridge, 12 cartridges per carton
    - Shelf life: 24 months from the date of production
2.10 Storage conditions. The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +25°C. Always refer to packaging. Refer to the current Safety Data Sheet for information on safe handling and storage.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation. The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, old sealants and poorly bonded coatings which could affect adhesion of the primer and sealant. The substrate should be of sufficient strength to withstand with the stress induced by the sealant during movement. Use techniques such as wire brushing, grinding, grit blasting or other suitable mechanical methods to remove all weak substrate material. Repair all damaged joint edges with suitable Sika® repair products. Remove all dust, loose and friable material from all surfaces before application.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Backing material: Use polyethylene foam backing rods
4.3 Consumption.
    | Joint width | Joint depth | Joint length per | Joint length per |
    | 300ml cartridge | 600ml foil pack |
    | 10 mm | 10 mm | 3.00 lm | 1.50 lm |
    | 20 mm | 10 mm | 1.50 lm | 3.00 lm |
    | 30 mm | 15 mm | 0.65 lm | 1.30 lm |
    | 40 mm | 20 mm | 0.38 lm | 0.75 lm |
    | 50 mm | 25 mm | 0.24 lm | 0.48 lm |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Curing rate.
    | ~2.0mm / 24 hours | At +23°C / 50% R.H. |
    Test method printed: (CQP 049-2)
4.5 Skinning time.
    | ~15 minutes | At +23°C / 50 % R.H. |
    Test method printed: (CQP 019-1)
4.6 Application method / tools.
    - Strictly follow installation procedures as defined in Method Statements, application manuals and working instructions which must always be adjusted to the actual site conditions.
    - Masking
    - It is recommended to use masking tape where neat or exact joint lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time after finishing.
4.7 Application method / tools - Joint Backing.
    - After the required substrate preparation, insert a suitable backing rod to the required depth.
    - Application
    - Prepare the end of the cartridge / foil pack before or after inserting into the sealant gun then fit the nozzle. Extrude Sika® Firerate into the joint ensuringthat it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoiding any air entrapment.
    - Finishing
    - As soon as possible after application, sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion and a smooth finish. Do not use tooling products containing solvents.
4.8 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use with water. Once cured, residual material can only be re-moved mechanically.
4.9 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not use Sika® Firerate on damp and/or wet substrates.
    - Do not apply Sika® Firerate at temperatures below 5°C.
    - Do not use Sika® Firerate to seal joints in and around swimming pools.
    - Do not use Sika® Firerate to seal joints in external applications on nonporous substrates.
    - Do not use Sika® Firerate for joints under water pressure or for permanent water immersion.
    - Do not expose uncured Sika® Firerate to rain or water as this may interfere with the curing reaction.
    - Sika® Firerate can be overpainted with most conventional water-based coating and paint systems. However, paints must first be tested to ensure compatibility by carrying out preliminary trials. The best over-painting results are obtained when the adhesive is allowed to fully cure first. Note: Non-flexible paint systems may impair the elasticity of the adhesive and lead to cracking of the paint film.
4.10 Further documentation - Further documents.
    - AS 1530.4:2014 test report
    - AS/ISO 717.4:2004 test report
    - Sika® Passive fire protection solutions

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature.
    | Maximum | +40°C |
    | Minimum | +5°C |
5.3 Substrate temperature.
    | Maximum | +35°C |
    | Minimum | +5°C |
    Note: The Substrate temperature must be +3°C above dew point temperature and free from frost and ice.
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.9):
    - Do not apply Sika® Firerate at temperatures below 5°C.
    - Do not expose uncured Sika® Firerate to rain or water as this may interfere with the curing reaction.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Shore A hardness: ~30 (after 28 days) (EN ISO 868)
    - Curing rate: ~2.0mm / 24 hours | At +23°C / 50% R.H. (CQP 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~15 minutes | At +23°C / 50 % R.H. (CQP 019-1)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Firerate, July 2025, Version 01.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/3/sika_firerate.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sika® Firerate, version 22/07/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/Sika%20Firerate.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® Firerate, version 24/02/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/sds-sika-firerate.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
